def factor_range_expansion_reversal(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    range_ = df_copy["high"] - df_copy["low"]
    lookback = 50
    mean_range = range_.rolling(lookback, min_periods=lookback).mean()
    std_range = range_.rolling(lookback, min_periods=lookback).std()
    range_z = (range_ - mean_range) / std_range.replace(0, np.nan)
    ret5 = df_copy["close"].pct_change(5)
    raw = -ret5 * range_z
    ema_signal = raw.ewm(span=3, min_periods=3).mean()
    df_copy["factor_range_expansion_reversal"] = ema_signal
    return df_copy["factor_range_expansion_reversal"]
description: This factor captures volatility expansion and subsequent mean-reversion. It measures current range (high‑low) relative to its historical distribution via a rolling z-score, then multiplies by the negative 5-day return. Thus, a large drop accompanied by a spike in daily range produces a high positive signal, anticipating a reversal. The final signal is smoothed with an EMA(3) to reduce noise while preserving responsiveness. This combines range-based volatility expansion with return-based reversal, consistent with the Price-Volatility Behavior layer.
